description: Flexible business-class fare radar policy. Config, never code: home airports, destination watchlists, date-window generation, quality filters, the deterministic deal score and the hard request budget all live here. No airport, destination or exchange of money is ever hard-coded into search logic.

homeAirports.note: PRIMARY airports always compete in every run; EXTENDED join only when extendedEnabled (or --extended). The engine treats the list as data — adding BER/WAW later is a config edit, not a redesign. Fare differences between home airports are EXPOSED, never converted into a positioning cost (no factual ground-transport data exists yet).

watchlists.note: ANYWHERE mode = the union of every watchlist, honestly labelled: no cash provider we use supports true destination-less discovery, so 'anywhere' means 'everywhere we have chosen to look'. Lists are config; a new region is a new key.

window.note: preferredNights are the trip lengths the refinement tier actually tests — never a blind cartesian product, and never an assumed fixed 7.

quality.note: Itineraries over maxStops/maxDuration are dropped with the drop counted in the run plan. LONG_LAYOVER and OVERNIGHT_CONNECTION are recorded flags that feed the value score and the UI — a cheap nightmare must say WHY it is cheaper. Self-transfer/separate-ticket flags are carried in the schema but our current providers only quote single-ticket itineraries, so they never fire today (data, not guesswork).

scoring.description: Deterministic and price-dominant; no model, no opacity. dealScore = 100 × (cheapest qualifying fare in the result set ÷ this fare) minus fixed penalties. The raw CHEAPEST ordering is always available untouched beside BEST VALUE.
scoring.note: businessMixed at 10 means a mixed-cabin fare must be ~10% cheaper before it outranks full business on value; premiumEconomyAsResult at 100 removes any non-business echo from value ranking entirely (it stays visible, labelled, in the raw list).

budget.note: Hard ceiling per run, planned BEFORE any request and printed as a visible plan. All tiers use the FREE provider (fast_flights) — politeness-capped, zero billing; the metered SerpAPI provider is NEVER touched by the radar (allowMeteredFallback:false everywhere), so the production flight budget cannot be dented. When the plan exceeds the cap, breadth reduces in order: fewer probes per route → fewer refinement cells → fewer destinations, and every reduction is named in the plan. For ONE_WAY runs refineNightsVariants buys neighbour DATES per cell instead of trip-length variants (a one-way has no trip length) — the arithmetic and the cap are identical. Currency EUR to match the market layer's comparison currency; flight_prices rows record it per-row (currency is a hard baseline dimension).

baselines.note: A 'typical fare' for (origin|destination|nights bucket|cabin|currency) is only quoted once this many observations across this many distinct days exist — until then the UI shows no deal-percentage, matching the stays/packages maturity doctrine.
